newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Sterling volatilities soar, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Sterling volatilities soar, but off highs.

text.p: Option implied volatilities for sterling, against both the dollar and the mark, were off early highs but stayed well bid in U.S. trading after the pound vaulted to fresh highs, dealers said.
"With the move to $1.65 (in spot cable), vols got bid really aggressively," said a trader at a U.S. bank in Chicago.
Cable earlier in the day rose to a 20-month high of $1.6560 and sterling/mark to a 2-1/2 high of 2.5030 marks, triggering waves of short-covering in both spot sterling and options.
One-month cable implied volatility stood at 8.5/8.8 percent in late in the U.S. afternoon, off from early highs around nine percent, but well above late Monday's 8.3/8.7.

"We haven't seen these levels in sterling for years," said Kyoko Hiramatsu, a senior trader at Bank of Yokohama in New York. She noted, however, that the volatility curve was inverted in the intermediate portion as most of the curve had not shot up as much as the front end.
Three-month cable was at 8.2/8.5 percent, below the one-month volatility, which has gained more than a full point in the past two days.
"I think a lot of people are still skeptical how long this bullishness could last," Hiramatsu said.
Still, the Chicago trader said demand for sterling calls were likely to stay robust because most people did not have strike prices much above current spot levels in their books.
One-month sterling/mark volatility stood at 8.4/8.9 percent, a quarter point higher than Monday's closing levels.
Trading in dollar/mark and dollar/yen options was relatively quiet as the spot greenback meandered in familiar territories and traders awaited the outcome of U.S. elections.
One-month dollar/mark gained a quarter point to 7.8/8.0 percent, while one-month dollar/yen was little changed at 8.2/8.4 percent.

Although the spot dollar climbed toward 114.30 yen in U.S. trading, dealers said it looked toppish and volatilities were unlikely to see strong bidding unless the U.S. currency threatened to break above last week's highs just below 115 yen.
Hiramatsu said some Japanese traders were starting to refocus on the dollar's downside risk.
Risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, were largely unchanged. One-month 25-delta dollar/yen was at 0.0/0.3 percent in favor of yen calls.

Elsewhere, dollar/Swiss franc volatilities were well bid as the spot dollar climbed to a fresh 20-month high. Although the dollar appeared to be on a bullish trend, concerns over how Russian President Boris Yeltsin would recover from a heart surgery were underpinning the safe-haven Swiss currency and option volatilities, trader said.
One-month dollar/Swiss volatility stood at 9.3/9.5 percent, a touch higher than late Monday levels.
